newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Court asked to stop takeover of Manila water firm.
newsitem.headline: Court asked to stop takeover of Manila water firm.

text.p: Workers on Thursday asked the Philippine Supreme Court to stop the privatisation of the capital's water utility, saying the deal was unlawful.

In a petition filed with the court, the workers said water "is part of our national patrimony" and that under the constitution, the development and use of natural resources comes under full control and supervision of the state.
The government in February awarded two foreign and locally-owned consortiums 25-year concessions to run the city's Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS).
The consortium of Ayala Corp, Bechtel Corp of the United States and United Utilities won the contract for the east zone of Manila. The west zone was won by Benpres Holdings and Lyonnaise des Eaux SA.
The protest was filed by three organisations representing MWSS employees, other civil servants and leftist unions.
It was the latest of number of legal challenges filed by various groups against government efforts to privatise state-owned or state-run agencies.

The Supreme Court in February stirred a political storm when it stopped the government from selling the 75-year-old Manila Hotel to the Malaysian firm Renong Bhd and ordered it sold to a local company. The court said the historic hotel was a national treasure.
Besides asking that the MWSS deal be nullified, the workers also asked the court to stop any mass termination of MWSS employees after privatisation.
Hundreds of MWSS workers last week staged walkouts to back their demands for a higher severance pay package in case their services were terminated.
Another private group earlier this year tried to stop the privatisation of the water utility but an appeals court dismissed the protest.
